newsitem.title: CROATIA: Stronger kuna demand pushes money market rate up.
newsitem.headline: Stronger kuna demand pushes money market rate up.

text.p: Stronger demand for kuna funds boosted the average Croatian money market rate to 9.4 percent on Tuesday from 8.3 percent.
Dealers said short-term interbank rates ranged from 9.0 for call money to 10 and 11 percent for term loans.
Insurer placements were also made at a new, higher rate of 8.0 percent, up one percentage point.
Budget and pension payments through commercial banks boosted their accounts, but today's trade left a slight shortfall after 45 million kuna were settled.
Monday's overnight loans totalled 35 million kuna as two banks borrowed money for mandatory reserves.

The central bank's kuna midrates for Wednesday's dealings firmed to 5.4346 from 5.4551 against the dollar and to 3.5632 from 3.5645 to the German mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
